claim_reviews.note: The induction keeps the remainder on the correct side: W(1+Y)+binom(a,2). Only powers of one element occur, so no ring commutativity is used.
Both cancellations were recomputed. For q=p the remaining exponents are cp^(k+1) and p^(2k+1); for q!=p, Bezout and localness make q a unit. The proof uses p odd, not ell>n or n! invertibility.
The increasing chain (x/p^a) proves principal-ideal separation in the given Noetherian domain. Prime-order induction then handles every positive finite order, with all powers still congruent to one.

The discriminant hypothesis makes the regular trace pairing modulo p nondegenerate; every nilpotent is orthogonal to all elements, so the finite algebra is reduced. Localization yields maximal ideal (p). Integral-basis finiteness, dimension-one normal local DVR structure and completion are explicitly matched at the supplied place.

Literal Kc(1) is the image of integral invertible matrices reducing to identity modulo the maximal ideal. NTL4 justifies replacing that ideal by (p); injectivity transfers finite order to the integral lift, so NTL3 applies.
Compactness gives finitely many left cosets of the open subgroup K intersect KO. Equality of two cosets represented by powers gives a positive integral power without requiring normality.
Characteristic coefficients commute with the completion embedding and are invariant under conjugation. The same conjugating element works for the inverse since KO is a subgroup.

Restriction of local valuations preserves their sign. The denominator-ideal proof supplies local-to-global integrality, and x+conj(x), x*conj(x) in the maximal real field give the original quadratic integral equation. This covers an arbitrary selected place above each v.

Degree and elementary symmetric bounds leave only finitely many integral minimal polynomials. Every conjugate extends to the given number field, so the asserted bounded-integral finiteness is proved without importing geometry of numbers.

Cayley-Hamilton places every nonnegative power in one bounded-denominator module. The actual CM involution gives complex unitarity at every embedding; finite possible entries force two powers to agree and hence finite order.

The inverse matrix is the transpose of the CM-conjugate matrix. Its characteristic coefficients are the conjugates of those of M, and the same compact local conjugate supplies both integrality conditions needed by NTL8.

Literal ratU is the rational GL image inside the identity-Hermitian adelic group UA. The rational involution equation descends through the injective diagonal field map, and all cLoc coordinates and all powers remain those of the same M.
